title: Year-to-year weather did not explain the terrestrial insect decline or the freshwater increase in the global InsectChange database (1952-2019); a same-year warmth link occurred only in observer counts
abstract: Question: do year-to-year weather anomalies explain changes and long-term trends of insect abundance in the global InsectChange database, and is a same-year link a sampling effect? Data: 1,208 series from 99 unmanipulated data sources (663 terrestrial series from 62 sources, 545 freshwater series from 37 sources), 1952-2019 (InsectChange 2025 file, CC BY 4.0), with GHCN-CAMS temperature and CRU TS 4.09 precipitation at each plot. Method: a plan was written before outcome models. Within-series models removed series x period effects and a separate linear trend for each series; terms were warm half-year temperature of the same and previous year, prior cold half-year temperature and warm half-year rain. Intervals are 95% data-source cluster bootstrap. Results: pooled same-year temperature links were not clear (terrestrial +2.4% per 1 C, -4.6 to +8.4; freshwater +2.5%, -4.1 to +14.4); hot and dry half-years had no clear links. Only terrestrial observer counts (16 sources, mostly butterfly transects) had a clear same-year link (+10.8% per 1 C, +4.9 to +14.8), repeated in Europe and North America, with no next-year carry-over and a null next-year placebo. Traps and area samples showed no clear link. The terrestrial mean trend was -1.09% per year (-2.12 to -0.08), but the weather-implied trend was +0.05% per year; the freshwater trend was +1.80% per year, with +0.21% implied. A decline of that size from warming would need about -31% per 1 C. Limitations: half-year gridded weather does not measure sampling-day weather; method and taxon are confounded; few sources in several subgroups; air pollution was not tested.

display.caption: Change in insect abundance per +1 C of warm half-year temperature in the same year, the previous year and the next year (placebo), by realm and sampling class. Lines are 95% data-source cluster bootstrap intervals. Open points have fewer than 10 data sources.

Left: mean observed trend per data source and the trend implied by the weather sensitivities and local weather trends. Right: implied versus observed trend for each data source; the y axis is clipped at +/-12% per year.
